title: Mad Libs Story
story: Remember playing Mad Libs? You ask a friend for 'a silly name,' 'an adjective,' 'a noun,' and 'a verb' — then you plug those words into a story and it comes out hilariously weird. Let's build our own Mad Libs generator where YOU supply the words and the program creates the story!
why: Mad Libs teaches you to think of variables as placeholders. Each blank is a variable, and when you fill them in, the story comes to life. This is exactly how templates work in real apps — from email greetings to personalized websites.
analogy: A Mad Lib is like a fill-in-the-blank worksheet — the story structure stays the same, but you can swap in any words to make it funny, weird, or completely unhinged.
try_it: Make the story even crazier! Change all four words and see how the story transforms. Add a fifth variable — maybe an `animal` or a `place` — and weave it into the story. Can you make the story rhyme? What's the funniest combination you can create?
tips: Think of variables as blank slots in your story — you fill them in once and the story uses them everywhere.
Break long sentences into smaller pieces and concatenate step by step — each `string.str_concat` adds one more word.
Add spaces inside your strings: `"found a "` has a space at the end so the next word doesn't stick to 'a'.
Use empty `io.println("")` to print blank lines between parts of your story for better readability.
common_mistakes: Forgetting spaces between words: `string.str_concat(adjective, noun)` produces `sparklytoaster` instead of "sparkly toaster".
Trying to pass more than two arguments: `string.str_concat(a, b, c)` doesn't work — chain multiple calls instead.
